questions.stem: Each paired schematic contrasts normal circulation with a distinct triggering insult. Despite the differing initiating events, what final common physiologic derangement do all of these depicted states share?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An increase in cardiac output in every case

choices.label: B
choices.text: A rise in systemic vascular resistance in every case

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inadequate tissue perfusion and oxygen delivery

choices.label: D
choices.text: An elevation of central venous pressure in every case

choices.label: E
choices.text: A primary respiratory alkalosis in every case

explanation.summary: The panels illustrate the initiating insult of the five shock types, but all forms of shock converge on failed delivery of oxygen to the tissues, producing cellular hypoxia regardless of the upstream cause.
explanation.whyCorrect: The panels illustrate the initiating insult of the five shock types, but all forms of shock converge on failed delivery of oxygen to the tissues, producing cellular hypoxia regardless of the upstream cause.

questions.stem: In this pattern afterload rises while preload and cardiac output both fall. Which type of shock is depicted?

explanation.summary: Loss of intravascular volume drops venous return (preload) and cardiac output, while compensatory sympathetic vasoconstriction raises systemic vascular resistance (afterload) to defend the mean arterial pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of intravascular volume drops venous return (preload) and cardiac output, while compensatory sympathetic vasoconstriction raises systemic vascular resistance (afterload) to defend the mean arterial pressure.

questions.stem: Here preload, afterload, and cardiac output all decline together. Which type of shock does this reflect?

explanation.summary: Loss of sympathetic tone after cord or brain injury causes vasodilation (falling afterload and preload) without the compensatory tachycardia seen in other shocks, so cardiac output falls as well, producing hypotension with bradycardia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Loss of sympathetic tone after cord or brain injury causes vasodilation (falling afterload and preload) without the compensatory tachycardia seen in other shocks, so cardiac output falls as well, producing hypotension with bradycardia.
